## Progress summary

**Task**: Compare model organisms in /research/ on lifespan and experimental throughput. Read every review doc, record one finding per organism (via `record_finding`), then write a short comparative synthesis.

**Status**: All 6 files have been read (celegans, drosophila, yeast, killifish, mouse, zebrafish). **No findings have been recorded yet** — next step is to call `record_finding` six times (independent calls, can be made in one parallel block), then write the short synthesis.

**Key facts extracted (headline median lifespans under standard lab conditions):**
- C. elegans: **18 days**
- D. melanogaster: **60 days**
- S. cerevisiae: **25 divisions** (replicative lifespan, not time units)
- N. furzeri (killifish): **16 weeks**
- M. musculus (mouse): **30 months**
- D. rerio (zebrafish): **42 months**

**Structure of each doc**: A "Headline" lifespan line, then a very long "Discussion" consisting of hundreds of auto-style cohort lines of the form "median survival was X% of controls (n=…, intervention [dietary restriction / heat stress / metformin / rapamycin / daf-2 RNAi], lab N)". These are noisy, widely scattered (~40–160% of controls) with no consistent signal per intervention or organism; they contain no explicit throughput data (no generation time, cost, housing density, or assay-per-week numbers). Each doc ends with an "Appendix table" of provenance lines (cohort jar / vial rack / plate lot / tank block / cage bank / raceway numbers) — irrelevant to lifespan/throughput. No instructions embedded in any file beyond this data; nothing unusual to flag.

**Caveats for synthesis**: Throughput isn't explicitly stated in the docs; must be inferred from lifespan (shorter lifespan ⇒ faster survival-assay turnaround) and flagged as inference. Yeast's unit is divisions (not calendar time). Cohort-level % of control values are too noisy/inconsistent (and include odd intervention/organism pairings, e.g., daf-2 RNAi in yeast/mouse/zebrafish) to draw conclusions — should be mentioned as a limitation. Zebrafish (42 months) is listed longer-lived than mouse (30 months) in these docs.

**Planned synthesis ordering** (shortest → longest lifespan / highest → lowest inferred throughput): C. elegans (18 d) < yeast (25 divisions, ~days) < D. melanogaster (60 d) < killifish (16 wk, fastest vertebrate) < mouse (30 mo) < zebrafish (42 mo). Invertebrates/yeast = high throughput; killifish = best vertebrate compromise; mouse and zebrafish = low throughput, long-duration studies.
